versions.short: The bill would let the Secretary of the Interior make a one-time agreement lasting up to five years with the Gateway Arch Park Foundation, a nonprofit partner of the Gateway Arch National Park, so the foundation could host private events at the park, including in certain park buildings such as the Arch Visitor Center and the Old Courthouse. The agreement would have to protect the park, limiting the number of events each month, setting staffing levels for safety, requiring liability insurance naming the United States as an additional insured, and shielding the federal government from liability for injuries or deaths linked to the foundation's use of the buildings. Events would have to fit the park's purposes, avoid damaging it, and not disrupt public access, and the Secretary would charge fees to cover wear and tear and could recover the costs of the events. The National Park Service could still host its own events and issue permits to others, and the authority would end seven years after enactment. The Secretary would also have to report to Congress within four years on how the arrangement affects visitors, security, staffing, and finances.
